tagline: Once around Lake Winnipesaukee, the long way.
intro: From Alton Bay, the four-mile cove at the lake's south end, NH 11 runs up the western side of Lake Winnipesaukee through Gilford, past Mount Major and Ellacoya State Park, with the Ossipee Range across the water. At The Weirs, the lake's outlet, where the Winnipesaukee people lived and fished and the colonists found weirs, the road goes on to Meredith, then turns onto NH 25 for Center Harbor and Moultonborough and the less developed eastern side.

Lake steamers, forerunners of the MS Mount Washington, began calling at Alton Bay in 1872, and the Mount Washington made its main summer port on the boulevard at Weirs Beach, across the street from the arcades.

moments.title: Endicott Rock
moments.text: In 1652 surveyors for the Massachusetts Bay Colony cut Governor Endicott's name into a rock here, mistaking the spot for the head of the Merrimack.

moments.title: Castle in the Clouds
moments.text: On a ledge of Lee Mountain above the lake, shoe millionaire Thomas Plant built a 16-room mansion in 1913 and 1914 and named it Lucknow, perhaps as a play on being in luck now.

moments.title: Wolfeboro
moments.text: Governor John Wentworth built his Kingswood estate beside Lake Wentworth in 1771, the first summer country estate in northern New England, and the town's motto is The Oldest Summer Resort in America.
